theme: Performance and stability on Skia m151
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 brings Skia m151, broad managed-code performance wins, and a native resource leak fix.
highlights_body: Across SKColor, SKPMColor, SKFourByteTag, HarfBuzzSharp buffers, and SKShaper glyph reads, hot-path allocations and P/Invoke round-trips have been replaced with managed integer math and zero-copy spans. A long-standing native resource leak in `SKImage.FromEncodedData` with a crop rect is also resolved.

bullets.detail: The bundled Skia engine advances to m151, incorporating upstream rendering fixes, text improvements, and stability patches from multiple chrome/m151 sync merges.
A CPU raster rendering regression introduced in an earlier sync was resolved by restoring `SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT`.
Parsing hex color strings now accepts `ReadOnlySpan<char>` in addition to `string`, avoiding allocations in hot parsing paths. Hex parsing itself was also made faster.
Pre-built WASM native assets compiled with Emscripten 5.0.6 (with the new `exnref` exception-handling ABI) are now included for .NET 11 targets.

bullets.lead: Native resource leak in `SKImage.FromEncodedData` with crop rect fixed
bullets.detail: When `SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI)` was called and decoding succeeded, the intermediate full image was never released. The handle is now freed correctly.
`GRContextOptions` no longer requires an `unsafe` compilation context; the surplus modifier has been removed.

bullets.lead: Hot-path P/Invoke eliminations across color and tag types
bullets.detail: `SKColor`↔`SKColorF` conversion, single-value `SKPMColor` premultiply/unpremultiply, and `SKFourByteTag.Parse` / `HarfBuzzSharp.Tag.Parse` are now pure managed integer math — no native calls on the hot path.

bullets.lead: SKShaper glyph results read via zero-copy spans
bullets.detail: The post-shaping glyph, cluster, and position arrays are now read directly from native memory via `Span<T>`, eliminating the intermediate managed array allocations on every `Shape` call.
The string-overload of `AddUtf8` now uses a pooled scratch buffer instead of allocating a `byte[]` per call, significantly reducing GC pressure in text-shaping loops.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: SKShaper zero-copy glyph reads, WASM submodule fix, and general binding improvements

preview_summaries.v4.151.0-rc.1.1: The release candidate delivered the Skia m151 stability syncs, the native resource leak fix in SKImage, the WASM Emscripten 5.0.6 assets, and the CPU raster regression fix.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.2.1: Preview 2 landed the broad performance sweep: SKColor hex overloads, HarfBuzzSharp allocation-free AddUtf8, zero-copy glyph reads in SKShaper, and the four managed hot-path eliminations.
preview_summaries.v4.151.0-preview.1.1: Preview 1 opened the 4.151 line on Skia m151 and resolved the WASM SK_BUILD_FOR_WASM redefinition warning.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1 ships three performance improvements: `Buffer.AddUtf8(string)` is now allocation-free via buffer pooling, `Tag.Parse` eliminates its per-call `char[4]` allocation, and SKShaper reads glyph results through zero-copy spans.
